# Investment Memorandum

## 1. Executive Summary

- On March 8, 2024, BGC Group, Inc. (a Delaware corporation) and Cantor Fitzgerald, L.P. (a Delaware limited partnership) entered into a Second Amendment to their existing Credit Agreement.
- The original Credit Agreement was established on March 19, 2018 between BGC Partners, Inc. and Cantor, with BGC Group assuming all rights and obligations from BGC Partners, Inc. on October 6, 2023.
- This amendment modifies the intercompany credit facility between these affiliated financial services entities, establishing a $400 million aggregate lending limit and revising the interest rate structure.
- The amendment updates the "Applicable Rate" definition to reference rates from each party's respective revolving credit facilities with Bank of America, N.A., minus 25 basis points, and establishes clearer loan and repayment terms.

## 2. Investment Highlights & Risks

### Key Strengths / Credit Positives:
- Intercompany facility between established financial services entities with existing third-party banking relationships with Bank of America, N.A.
- Flexible borrowing structure allowing for borrowing, repayment, and reborrowing prior to maturity
- Interest rate mechanism tied to external revolving credit facilities provides market-based pricing discipline
- Amendment confirms all representations and warranties remain true and correct, indicating continued creditworthiness

### Principal Risks and Mitigating Factors:
- Intercompany nature of the facility creates potential concentration risk between affiliated entities
- Lender discretionary approval required for loans ("in its sole discretion"), which may limit borrowing certainty
- Mandatory prepayment provisions allow lender to demand repayment with only three business days' notice
- Limited visibility into the underlying financial condition or covenant structure of the borrowing entities

| **Deal Price** | N/A |

| **Maturity Date** | N/A |
| **Payment Frequency** | N/A |
| **Key Covenants** | • Aggregate principal amount of all loans outstanding shall not exceed $400 million at any time<br>• Lender may demand repayment with three business days' prior written notice<br>• Borrower may prepay loans at any time with accrued interest plus any costs incurred by lender<br>• All representations and warranties must remain true and correct |

- Interest rate mechanism tied to external revolving credit facilities provides market-based pricing discipline
- Amendment confirms all representations and warranties remain true and correct, indicating continued creditworthiness

### Principal Risks and Mitigating Factors:
- Intercompany nature of the facility creates potential concentration risk between affiliated entities
- Lender discretionary approval required for loans ("in its sole discretion"), which may limit borrowing certainty
- Mandatory prepayment provisions allow lender to demand repayment with only three business days' notice
- Limited visibility into the underlying financial condition or covenant structure of the borrowing entities
